title: The routing document's read-change-write is one step across processes
request: The owner: keep going by priority until tonight's full gate; 22.6 left the routing lock within one process only.
spec: CAPTURE_AND_DECISION_DATA_PLAN.md 22.6: the routing document's read-change-write was locked within one process, not across processes.
plan: Read the routing stores and every read-change-write
An atomic change on both stores
A cross-process test, and the tests on PostgreSQL

decisions.decision: A file lock beside the routing file; an advisory lock in one transaction on PostgreSQL
decisions.why: each store's own way to hold one writer at a time across processes

decisions.decision: The writer's checks run inside the lock
decisions.why: a check on a document another process changes meanwhile decides on stale facts

change: dclab_rnd/models/routing.py (atomic, FileRouting.change, PgRouting.change; the serve or shadow switch and the cap through it), dclab_rnd/ledger/routing.py (the decision switch through it), tests/test_routing_lock.py, the 22.6 plan status.

findings.scenario: change took the store's lock and called save, which took the same lock again
findings.cause: the store's lock was not re-entrant

findings.defect: The helper's name hid an existing function
findings.scenario: the module already had a change function further down
spawned children under unittest re-ran the test module
findings.cause: the test's design, not the lock

outcome: Four processes adding to the routing document at once lose no change; the serve, shadow, cap and decision switches all go through one locked step on files and on PostgreSQL.
lessons: A lock taken in a method that calls another locked method must be re-entrant.
Run checks inside the lock that guards the write.
risks: The lock file is advisory: a writer that bypasses atomic is not held.
